metaphor.sentence: Questions, family needs and the money assemble into a calm decision landscape — at the gentlest pace on this site, because this is the decision that deserves it.

proposition: The law gives a resident 15 working days to be sure. assembling turns that window into preparation — the money in plain words, the family's questions answered once, the lawyer briefed — so the decision is made inside the window, not despite it.

wait.moment: the 15 working days after you sign the Occupation Right Agreement

duration.note: An ORA must allow cancellation without reason for 15 working days after signing. Independent legal advice is mandatory under s 27 and must be certified.

wait.whyItExists: Parliament decided this decision is too big to be rushed: a licence to occupy, a deferred management fee, a family's next chapter. The window exists so a resident can be sure — with their own lawyer, by law.
wait.todayItFeelsLike: A tour, a brochure, a legal document — then a fortnight in which the biggest questions finally surface, after everyone has gone home.

asks: One question at a time, at conversation pace — “What matters most about the move: the garden, the dog, or being near Kāpiti Health Centre?”
“Who else should see the answers — just Sue, or the whole family?”
learns: Which questions the family actually has, gathered from everyone allowed in.
Which of those the documents already answer, and which need the village.
What the money means in dollars on this villa, not in defined terms.
prepares: The money in plain words: the deferred management fee in dollars, the weekly fee and its cap, the deposit and who holds it.
One brief for the independent lawyer, with the family's open questions attached.
The calendar: which working day of the window it is, and what remains open.
resolves: The repeat questions — each one answered once, visibly, for everyone the resident allowed.
The scattered paperwork — one file, and it belongs to the resident.

reward.headline: A decision made with your eyes open, inside the window.
reward.detail: By the lawyer's appointment, the resident and their family hold one plain-words sheet: what this villa costs to live in, what leaving costs, what the law protects, and which questions are still open. The certificate the law requires gets signed over understanding, not over trust.

permission.consent: You enquired, and you chose to be walked through the decision. The agent prepares; it never persuades.
reads: The Occupation Right Agreement you were given
The village's published fees for this villa
The questions you and your whānau raise
hardStops: It never advises on the ORA — the law reserves that for your own lawyer.
It never contacts the village on your behalf without your yes.
It never treats silence as a decision — the window closes by your word or not at all.
permission.retention: The working file belongs to the resident and leaves with them, whichever way they decide.

human.gateAt: before signing means anything — their certificate is required by law
human.whyStatutory: Retirement Villages Act 2003, s 27(3)–(6) — independent legal advice is mandatory, and the lawyer must witness the signature and certify on the prescribed form.

primary.metric: decisions settled inside the statutory window
primary.mechanism: Families reach the lawyer prepared, so the 15 working days hold a decision instead of a scramble — and fewer settled decisions unravel later.

secondary.mechanism: Each question is answered once, visibly, for everyone the resident allowed to see it.

evidencePack.example: the ORA as issued, Summerset's published fee schedule, the family's questions
worked examples use the villa's listed price; resale timing is stated as unknown, because no statutory deadline exists today
the lawyer added two questions about the weekly fee after termination
the resident's own lawyer — certificate under s 27, witnessed, day 9 of 15

persona.name: Margaret
persona.context: 78, deciding on a two-bedroom villa with her daughter Sue. ORA signed Tuesday — the 15 working days are running.

steps.showsCustomer: It is day 2 of your 15 working days. Nothing is final until your own lawyer certifies it — that is the law, and this window is yours. Shall we get the questions out of everyone's heads and into one place?
steps.doesBehind: Opens the family file and starts the window calendar. Reads the ORA as issued. Contacts nobody.
steps.question: Start gathering the questions?

steps.showsCustomer: Sue asked three questions overnight. Two are answered in the documents you already have — here they are in plain words. One is for the village: can the garden bed come with you?
steps.doesBehind: Deduplicates the family's questions, answers what the ORA and fee schedule already answer, and routes only the genuine unknowns — once.
steps.question: Send the garden question to the village?

steps.showsCustomer: The money, in dollars on this villa: the deferred management fee builds to 25% over four years. The weekly fee can only rise with the after-tax NZ Super increase. The $3,000 deposit sits with the statutory supervisor, not the village. What leaving costs is the honest hard part — repayment happens on relicensing, and no law sets its deadline today.
steps.doesBehind: Turns every defined term into a worked example on the actual price. States the exit uncertainty plainly instead of rounding it away — the reform debate is public and unfinished.
steps.question: Anything here you want worked through again?

steps.showsCustomer: Putting the lawyer's brief together — the plain-words money sheet, the family's open questions, and the village's answers so far. Slowly is fine. The window has thirteen days left.
steps.doesBehind: Assembles one brief. The pace is deliberate: this vertical gets the longest pauses on the site, because the decision deserves them.

steps.approving: the whole decision — the law requires independent legal advice, witnessed and certified, before the signature stands
steps.showsCustomer: Everything stops here, by law. Your lawyer — yours, not the village's — reads the brief, advises you alone, and certifies on the prescribed form. Nothing any agent did can substitute for this.
steps.doesBehind: Nothing. The hold is the point. The page itself goes still.
steps.question: Take the brief to your lawyer's appointment?

steps.showsCustomer: Decided inside the window, with six days to spare — and everything that informed it is in one file that belongs to you, whichever way you had decided.
steps.doesBehind: Writes the evidence pack: what was read, what was asked, what the village answered, what the lawyer changed, and the certificate reference.

evidence.claim: An Occupation Right Agreement must allow cancellation without reason for 15 working days after signing.
evidence.soWhat: The window this page is built on is not a design choice. It is the statute, and the design's job is to fill it with preparation instead of anxiety.

evidence.claim: Independent legal advice on an ORA is mandatory — the lawyer must witness the signature and certify on the prescribed form.
evidence.soWhat: The human gate here is not assembl's policy. It is Parliament's. The agent prepares the brief; only the resident's own lawyer can carry the decision.

evidence.claim: Roughly 130 people move into a New Zealand retirement village every week, and more than 53,000 live in one now.
evidence.soWhat: The window is running for dozens of families every week. Whoever fills it with the best preparation earns the confident decisions.

evidence.claim: Average capital repayment after leaving a village runs about 5.5 months, and reform announced in December 2025 — repayment within 12 months, interest after 6 — would not apply retrospectively.
evidence.source: 1News reporting; Retirement Commission on the announced reform
evidence.soWhat: The exit is the hard conversation. This page has it before signing, in plain words — because honesty now prevents grief later.

evidence.claim: Making the work visible increases how much people value the result — across five experiments, users preferred a slower service that showed its effort.
evidence.source: Buell & Norton, “The Labor Illusion”, Management Science 57(9)
evidence.soWhat: A fortnight that shows its preparation is a fortnight a family trusts. The pace of this page is the argument.

beforeWhileAfter.before: A tour, a brochure, then a legal document — and a fortnight in which the biggest questions finally surface, after everyone has gone home. Some families let the window close undecided.
beforeWhileAfter.while: The window becomes preparation: the money in dollars on the actual villa, every family question answered once, the lawyer's brief assembling at conversation pace.
beforeWhileAfter.after: The resident reaches the lawyer the law requires with one plain-words brief. The certificate is signed over understanding — and the decision holds, because it was truly made.

explainer.heading: what a monetised wait state actually is
explainer.standfirst: Nobody has a word for this yet, so here it is drawn out. Four panels, about a minute.
explainer.definition: A monetised wait state is a wait that pays for itself — you get something useful out of it, and the business gets work done that would otherwise cost it money later.

panels.title: the wait you already have
panels.caption: The law holds this window open on purpose: 15 working days to be sure. Today most of it passes in worry, not preparation.

panels.title: what the gap costs
panels.caption: Questions surface after everyone has gone home. The same one gets asked four ways. Some families let the window close undecided.

panels.title: what fills it
panels.caption: assembling turns the window into preparation — the money in dollars, the questions answered once, the lawyer's brief assembled at the family's pace.

panels.title: who is better off
panels.caption: The resident decides with their eyes open and the decision holds. The village welcomes residents who stay decided. The resident's own lawyer certifies it — that is the law.

textEquivalent: Start with the wait you already have. After signing an Occupation Right Agreement, the law gives the resident 15 working days to cancel without reason. Today that window mostly holds worry.
The window costs decisions. Questions surface late, get asked four ways, and some families let the fortnight close without truly deciding either way.
assembling fills the window with preparation: the money in dollars on the actual villa, every family question answered once, and one brief for the lawyer's appointment.

By the end, both sides are better off: the resident signs — or walks away — understanding the money, and the village gains residents whose decisions hold. The resident's own lawyer certifies it, as the law requires.
